## What you get back

Every reference gets a verdict, the record we matched it to, and a corrected citation in the style you picked. Errors are marked right in the reference, so you can see what to fix.

  1. Verified

LeCun, Y., Bengio, Y., & Hinton, G. (2015). Deep learning. Nature, 521(7553), 436–444.

Matches the published record in Nature. doi.org/10.1038/nature14539

  2. Mismatch

Kahneman, D., & Tversky, A. (~~1981~~1979). Prospect theory: An analysis of decision under risk. Econometrica, 47(2), 263–291.

The year in the record is 1979. Everything else matches.

  3. Retracted Matches record

Wakefield, A. J., Murch, S. H., Anthony, A., et al. (1998). Ileal-lymphoid-nodular hyperplasia, non-specific colitis, and pervasive developmental disorder in children. The Lancet, 351(9103), 637–641.

This paper exists, but The Lancet retracted it in 2010. Don't cite it as evidence.

  4. Couldn't verify

Martínez, L. (2020). Memoria y territorio en la poesía andina [Tesis de maestría]. Universidad Nacional.

No match found. This looks like a thesis, and most theses aren't in the databases we search. Try your library's catalog. This doesn't mean the source is made up.

# Bibliography checker

Paste a bibliography, reference list or Works Cited page. Numbers, bullets, page breaks and mixed styles are handled for you.

  * Reads numbered, bulleted and plain lists
  * Cleans up text pasted from PDFs
  * Export corrected citations as .docx, BibTeX or RIS
  * Free, no signup, nothing stored

Tip: some lines look like a title on its own. Add the author and year (for example: Achebe, C. (1958). Things fall apart. Heinemann.) for an accurate check.

Best format: Author. (Year). Title.

Up to 25 references. Numbering and bullets are fine. We don't store what you paste.

## What it does

Paste the whole list. The tool separates it into single references, looks each one up in Crossref, OpenAlex, DataCite, Open Library, Google Books and PubMed, and compares the record it finds with what you wrote. Each reference gets a verdict, the matched record, and a corrected citation in the style you pick. Retracted papers are flagged.

## What it can read

Lists come in many shapes, and a copied bibliography is rarely tidy. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Examples of Citations to Entire Bibliographies

Bibliographies are collections of references to the literature made for a specific purpose, such as to bring together references on a specific subject or by a particular author. Their citation format is identical to that of the standard book (see Chapter 2 for details) with three exceptions:

  * Authors are termed "compilers".

  * The content type "[bibliography]" is added after the title if the word is not part of the title. This alerts the user that the publication is not a standard book.

  * Descriptive information, such as the number of citations included, the sources searched, and the time period covered, may be added as notes to help the user identify the scope of the publication.

The chief source for information about a bibliography is its title page. The back of the title page, called the verso or copyright page, and the cover of the book are also sources of authoritative information.

References to bibliographies in print or in microform (microfilm, microfiche) are included in this chapter. For references to bibliographies in electronic form, see Chapter 18 and Chapter 22.

## FAQ

Are the DOIs/ISBNs or any file uploaded?

To fetch the metadata, only the DOI/ISBN identifier you enter is sent from your browser directly to a public API (CrossRef for DOIs, Google Books for ISBNs). No images, PDFs or manuscripts are ever uploaded. An identifier just names a published work — it is not personal information like a name or contact detail.

Which identifiers are supported? Can I use any URL?

Paper DOIs (identifiers starting with 10., or a doi.org URL) and book ISBNs (10 or 13 digits, hyphens allowed). Fetching metadata from an arbitrary web page URL is not supported, because browsers cannot read most pages directly. To cite a URL, use the manual Citation Formatter (citation) instead.

Which formats are supported? Can it output BibTeX or RIS?

APA (7th), MLA (9th), IEEE and SIST 02 (the Japanese standard), plus BibTeX and RIS. BibTeX drops into LaTeX, and RIS imports into EndNote, Mendeley, Zotero and similar managers. Changing the format does not re-fetch — it re-renders the records you already looked up in the new style.

Can I convert several references at once?

Yes. Paste one DOI or ISBN per line and press Convert to look them all up and format them together — handy for building a whole bibliography. Any line that cannot be found is flagged on its own line and does not affect the others.

Why might a lookup fail or a field be missing?

If the identifier is not in the source database, or the record there lacks fields such as volume, issue or pages, those parts are simply left blank. Each style also has finer rules (italics, abbreviating many authors), so check your final bibliography against the required style guide or a sample before submitting.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Citation Lookup

Find a specific journal article or book by the citation information.

If you have an article, book chapter, or book citation, use the Citation Lookup tool to search our journal and book holdings for full-text.  When the article/book/journal is immediately available through the library, options for access will be presented.  If it is not available for access, please use the “How to Get It” to request the item.

When searching for articles using citation elements, it is highly recommended to include:

  * Full title of the journal or its ISSN (do not use a journal abbreviation)
  * Year
  * Volume
  * Issue
  * Start page
  * A DOI or PMID

Please note: Articles published online ahead of print often lack citation information such as volume/issue/number.

When searching for books using citation elements, it is highly recommended to include:

  * Full title of the book or its ISBN
  * Author Last Name
  * Year
  * Volume

For assistance with finding full-text or searching for journal articles in one or more of our databases, please contact the Reference Desk.

A reference list should be ordered alphabetically by author’s surname unless you are using a numeric referencing system. In this case, sources are assigned a number when they first appear in the text, and are listed in numerical order.

#### Example reference list using the Harvard referencing style

Abu Salem, H., Gemail, K.S. and Nosair, A.M. (2021) 'A multidisciplinary approach for delineating wastewater flow paths in shallow groundwater aquifers: A case study in the southeastern part of the Nile Delta, Egypt', Journal of Contaminant Hydrology, 236, article number 103701. Available at: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jconhyd.2020.103701.

Ashbourn, J. (2014) Biometrics in the new world: the cloud, mobile technology and pervasive identity. 2nd edn. Springer.

Environment Agency (2020) The flood and coastal erosion risk management strategy action plan 2021. Environment Agency.

Mintel (2024) Sports and energy drinks - UK.  Available at: http://www.academic.mintel.com (Accessed: 5th June 2026).

Nasta, S. and Stein, M.U. (ed.) (2020) The Cambridge history of Black and Asian British writing. Cambridge University Press.

Tiwari, S. and Ambinakudige, S. (2020) 'Streetscapes and stereotyping: streets named after Martin Luther King, Jr., and the geographies of racial identity', GeoJournal, 87, pp. 921–934. Available at: https://doi.org/10.1007/s10708-020-10291-4.

World Health Organization (2025) Sodium reduction. Available at: https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/sodium-reduction (Accessed: 24 June 2026).

### Compiling a bibliography

Use a single list which integrates all the different types of source material you have used. The exception is where you have discussed a number of primary sources (such as novels, films, ancient sources, letters, historical documents etc), when you should separate your bibliography into primary and secondary sources. All lists should be ordered alphabetically by first-named author's surname or organisation if there is no named author.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Verify This Bibliography

Audit a reference list or manuscript before submission. CitationEasy checks local consistency first, then shows where identifier-backed metadata came from and flags strong disagreements for review.

This is an evidence report, not a correctness badge. It keeps manuscript text in your browser and never uses generative AI to invent or repair bibliographic data.

[Button: Try a sample]Verify metadata

## Local first

Document extraction, in-text matching, duplicates, and formatting checks run in your browser.

## Lookup source shown

Every resolved identifier names the registry or catalog used for the lookup.

## Uncertainty preserved

Unresolved and identifier-free references remain visibly unverified instead of being guessed.

## Frequently asked questions

What does the bibliography verifier check?
    It checks APA reference-list formatting, duplicate and ordering issues, author–date citations missing from the reference list, uncited references, identifier resolution, and strong title or year conflicts with retrieved metadata.

Is a resolved identifier proof that a citation is correct?
    No. Resolution only means the identifier returned metadata and no strong title or year conflict was detected. It does not prove that the source supports your claim, that it has not been corrected or retracted, or that every style detail is correct.

Is my manuscript uploaded?
    No. Word and text documents are read in your browser. Only extracted DOI, PMID, ISBN, or arXiv identifiers are sent for metadata lookup; manuscript prose is not sent.

Why was a reference not checked?
    The metadata pass needs a DOI, PMID, ISBN, or arXiv identifier. References without one still receive local formatting and manuscript cross-checks, but the tool does not guess whether an unidentifiable source exists.
